text: Given a valid GravityZone API key in X-Bitdefender-Api-Key, when bitdefender_list_policies is called, then it returns a paginated list of policy {id, name} objects matching GravityZone's getPoliciesList response shape.
Given per_page=500 is passed, when bitdefender_list_policies is called, then the effective per_page sent upstream is capped at 200, not passed through uncapped.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_list_policies_caps_per_page_at_200 -q -> 1 passed (2026-11-02); asserts the respx-captured JSON-RPC request body has params.perPage == 200

text: Given a real policy id, when bitdefender_get_policy_details is called against a live GravityZone tenant, then it returns that policy's configured modules, matching the GravityZone console for the same tenant.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key and a known policy id from the GravityZone console
Call bitdefender_get_policy_details with that policy id via a real tools/call
Open the same policy in the GravityZone console and compare module settings
expect: Tool response's module configuration matches what the GravityZone console shows for the same policy id

text: Given a valid API key, when bitdefender_list_endpoints is called, then it returns a paginated list of endpoint {id, name, status} objects.
Given a real endpoint id, when bitdefender_get_endpoint_details is called against a live GravityZone tenant, then it returns that endpoint's assigned policy and protection status.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key and a known endpoint id
Call bitdefender_get_endpoint_details with that endpoint id
Compare the returned assigned policy and protection status against the GravityZone console
expect: Returned assigned policy and protection status match the console for the same endpoint

text: Given a valid API key and no filters, when bitdefender_list_incidents is called, then it returns a paginated list of incident {id, name, priority, status} objects.
Given a tenant with zero open incidents, when bitdefender_list_incidents is called, then it returns an empty items array, not an error.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_list_incidents_empty_tenant_returns_empty_items -q -> 1 passed (2026-11-02); asserts items == [] and no "error" key

text: Given a real incident id, when bitdefender_get_incident is called against a live GravityZone tenant, then it returns that incident's affected endpoints and timeline summary.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key and a known incident id
Call bitdefender_get_incident with that incident id
Compare affected endpoints and timeline against the GravityZone console
expect: Returned affected endpoints and timeline summary match the console for the same incident

text: Given a real incident id and an allowed priority value, when bitdefender_change_incident_priority is called, then the incident's priority changes, confirmed by a follow-up bitdefender_get_incident call.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key and a known incident id
Call bitdefender_change_incident_priority with a new priority value
Call bitdefender_get_incident on the same incident id
expect: The follow-up get_incident call shows the new priority value

text: Given a real incident id and a GravityZone user id, when bitdefender_assign_incident is called, then the incident is reassigned, confirmed by a follow-up bitdefender_get_incident call.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key, a known incident id, and a valid GravityZone user id
Call bitdefender_assign_incident with that user id
Call bitdefender_get_incident on the same incident id
expect: The follow-up get_incident call shows the incident assigned to the given user id

text: Given a real endpoint id, when bitdefender_isolate_endpoint is called, then GravityZone creates an isolation task and the tool returns its task id; the tool is annotated destructiveHint.
steps: Obtain a GravityZone tenant API key and a known endpoint id (non-production/test endpoint)
Call bitdefender_isolate_endpoint with that endpoint id
Check the GravityZone console for the created isolation task and the tool's destructiveHint annotation in tools/list
expect: A task id is returned and the isolation task appears in the GravityZone console; tools/list marks the tool destructiveHint:true
notes: needs a real vendor account for the task round-trip; the destructiveHint:true half is already confirmed locally by tests/test_tools.py::test_tools_list_snapshot

text: Given a previously isolated endpoint id, when bitdefender_restore_endpoint_from_isolation is called, then GravityZone creates a restore task and the tool returns its task id.
steps: Using the endpoint isolated in TC11, call bitdefender_restore_endpoint_from_isolation
Check the GravityZone console for the created restore task
expect: A task id is returned and the restore task appears in the GravityZone console

text: Given no X-Bitdefender-Api-Key header is supplied, when any bitdefender_* tool is called, then it returns HTTP 401 with a body naming the missing header, not a 500.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_middleware.py::test_missing_api_key_header_returns_401_not_500 -q -> 1 passed (2026-11-02); also confirmed live via curl against the running server, see Self-test section in PRD-21222.md

text: Given GravityZone returns JSON-RPC error -32602 or HTTP 429, when a bitdefender_* tool receives it, then it maps to the structured error envelope with code invalid_argument or rate_limited respectively, never an unhandled exception or raw 500.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py -k 'maps_to' -q -> 3 passed (2026-11-02): -32602 -> invalid_argument, HTTP 429 (retries exhausted) -> rate_limited, HTTP 401 -> unauthorized

text: Given two concurrent requests using two different X-Bitdefender-Api-Key values, when each calls bitdefender_list_policies, then each response reflects only its own tenant's mocked data and the contextvar for request A is never visible while handling request B.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_credentials -q -> 1 passed (2026-11-02); asserts the two concurrently-gathered results carry two distinct Authorization headers and never cross

text: Given a mocked sequence of HTTP 429 responses followed by a 200, when a bitdefender_* tool call is retried, then it follows the bounded backoff policy and either succeeds or returns rate_limited, never hanging past the configured cap.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_tools.py::test_rate_limit_backoff_then_success -q -> 1 passed (2026-11-02); one mocked 429 then a 200, tool call succeeds with empty items, asyncio.sleep patched out so the test itself takes no real backoff delay
